pairs.label: Separate acceptance from delivery
pairs.detail: Commit the intent and outbox event before acknowledging it.
pairs.explanation: Commit the intent and outbox event before acknowledging it. Template rendering, scheduling, fanout, and provider calls continue asynchronously.

pairs.label: Recheck policy before send
pairs.detail: An enqueue-time decision can become stale.

pairs.label: Make retries harmless
pairs.detail: Use stable delivery and attempt identities across queues, workers, provider requests, and callbacks.
pairs.explanation: Use stable delivery and attempt identities across queues, workers, provider requests, and callbacks. At-least-once transport should still produce one logical send.

pairs.detail: Store tenant, idempotency key, event type, audience reference, template version, priority, schedule, payload reference, creation time, and cancellation state.
pairs.explanation: Store tenant, idempotency key, event type, audience reference, template version, priority, schedule, payload reference, creation time, and cancellation state. The unique tenant-key pair returns one stable notification ID.

pairs.label: Channel delivery

pairs.explanation: Store notification, recipient, channel, normalized destination reference, delivery state, policy version, send_after, suppression reason, and latest attempt sequence. Uniqueness prevents replayed fanout from creating a second logical send.

pairs.label: Provider attempt
pairs.detail: Store channel delivery, sequence, provider, stable idempotency key, request hash, start time, normalized outcome, provider message ID, retry time, and error class.
pairs.explanation: Store channel delivery, sequence, provider, stable idempotency key, request hash, start time, normalized outcome, provider message ID, retry time, and error class.

pairs.label: Policy and template versions
pairs.detail: Keep immutable template versions and auditable policy revisions.
pairs.explanation: Keep immutable template versions and auditable policy revisions. Record which versions produced a suppression or send without copying sensitive preference data into every event.

pairs.label: Load current policy
pairs.detail: Read the latest consent, category, channel, destination verification, quiet hours, frequency caps, and tenant policy.
pairs.explanation: Read the latest consent, category, channel, destination verification, quiet hours, frequency caps, and tenant policy. Fail closed for optional communication when policy cannot be established.

pairs.label: Schedule or suppress
pairs.detail: Persist a terminal suppression reason or a durable send_after time.
pairs.explanation: Persist a terminal suppression reason or a durable send_after time. Scheduled work is revalidated when due rather than trusting the old decision.

pairs.label: Render a pinned version
pairs.detail: Use the accepted template version, validate required variables, escape channel-specific content, and keep secrets or sensitive attributes out of queue payloads.
pairs.explanation: Use the accepted template version, validate required variables, escape channel-specific content, and keep secrets or sensitive attributes out of queue payloads.

pairs.label: Acquire quota
pairs.detail: Apply hierarchical token buckets for tenant, category, channel, provider account, sender identity, and destination.
pairs.explanation: Apply hierarchical token buckets for tenant, category, channel, provider account, sender identity, and destination. Reserve critical capacity without ignoring hard provider limits.

pairs.label: Call through an adapter
pairs.detail: Translate the canonical request to a provider API and normalize accepted, permanent, retryable, rate-limited, and unknown outcomes.
pairs.explanation: Translate the canonical request to a provider API and normalize accepted, permanent, retryable, rate-limited, and unknown outcomes.

pairs.label: Reconcile state
pairs.detail: Merge synchronous outcomes and signed callbacks by attempt identity.
pairs.explanation: Merge synchronous outcomes and signed callbacks by attempt identity. Emit monotonic delivery changes and schedule only bounded, policy-valid retries.

pairs.label: Queue partition or worker loss
pairs.detail: Reassign the partition and replay from the durable checkpoint.
pairs.explanation: Reassign the partition and replay from the durable checkpoint. Stable notification, delivery, and attempt IDs make duplicate consumption harmless.

pairs.label: Preference store unavailable
pairs.detail: Pause optional sends whose current eligibility cannot be proven.
pairs.explanation: Pause optional sends whose current eligibility cannot be proven. Use a narrowly defined, audited policy for critical transactional classes rather than a blanket bypass.

pairs.label: Provider outage
pairs.detail: Open the provider circuit, stop consuming quota, isolate its queue, and fail over only when sender identity, region, policy, and cost permit it.
pairs.explanation: Open the provider circuit, stop consuming quota, isolate its queue, and fail over only when sender identity, region, policy, and cost permit it.

pairs.label: Scheduler delay
pairs.detail: Scan overdue time buckets, reclaim expired leases, and prioritize by due time and class.
pairs.explanation: Scan overdue time buckets, reclaim expired leases, and prioritize by due time and class. A late schedule still requires a fresh policy check.

variants.context: A notification system turns a product event, such as an order update or security alert, into one or more messages delivered through email, SMS, push, or in-app channels. variants.prompt: From the lesson section “What trade-offs define this design?”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Async acceptance vs inline send
pairs.detail: Asynchronous delivery absorbs bursts and provider slowness but requires honest status APIs and eventual results.
pairs.explanation: Asynchronous delivery absorbs bursts and provider slowness but requires honest status APIs and eventual results. Inline send looks simple but couples caller latency and availability to every provider.

pairs.label: Revalidate vs freeze policy
pairs.detail: Send-time revalidation adds a preference read and race handling, but honors recent opt-outs.
pairs.explanation: Send-time revalidation adds a preference read and race handling, but honors recent opt-outs. Freezing the enqueue-time plan is cheaper and unsafe when work waits in queues.

pairs.label: Channel lanes vs one queue
pairs.detail: Channel and priority lanes scale and fail independently but require routing and fair scheduling.
pairs.explanation: Channel and priority lanes scale and fail independently but require routing and fair scheduling. One FIFO queue is easier until slow email or provider throttling delays critical push and SMS.

pairs.label: Adapters vs direct integration
pairs.detail: A canonical adapter contract adds translation code but standardizes outcomes, retries, metrics, and failover.
pairs.explanation: A canonical adapter contract adds translation code but standardizes outcomes, retries, metrics, and failover. Direct provider calls expose vendor details throughout the product and make safe migration harder.

pairs.label: Render late vs render early
pairs.detail: Late rendering uses current recipient data and avoids storing message bodies, but increases send-path work.
pairs.explanation: Late rendering uses current recipient data and avoids storing message bodies, but increases send-path work. Early rendering makes dispatch cheaper but can expose stale or sensitive content while queued.

pairs.label: Recipient rows vs lazy fanout
pairs.detail: Materialized rows simplify per-recipient audit and cancellation but amplify writes.
pairs.explanation: Materialized rows simplify per-recipient audit and cancellation but amplify writes. Checkpointed lazy expansion controls write bursts but makes aggregate progress and audience freshness more complex.

pairs.explanation: Store future send_after times durably, then route due work by priority, channel, provider, and tenant fairness boundaries.

pairs.label: Revalidate and render

pairs.explanation: Load current policy, suppress or reschedule when required, pin a template version, and acquire all applicable quotas.

pairs.label: Dispatch idempotently

pairs.explanation: Call a normalized provider adapter with a stable attempt key, bounded retries, circuit breaking, and policy-controlled failover.

pairs.label: Reconcile and operate
pairs.detail: Merge worker results and signed callbacks into monotonic state, alert on oldest eligible age, and audit policy, cost, and duplicate risk.
pairs.explanation: Merge worker results and signed callbacks into monotonic state, alert on oldest eligible age, and audit policy, cost, and duplicate risk.
